title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'digression B' (previous page), Grothendieck sets the stratified space aside and works with a general topological category Σ. Its object space is Σ(0) and its arrow space is Σ(1), with source s and target b from Σ(1) to Σ(0), and Σ(2) = (Σ(1),b) ×_{Σ(0)} (Σ(1),s) is the space of composable pairs. The motivating example is Σ(1) ⊂ Σ×Σ, the 'deployed' stratified space, where the arrows are the link/tube data between strata. He wants to recover the poset of strata intrinsically.

Claim. If the source or target map is a fibration, then I := π0(Σ(0)) carries a preorder. Its graph is the image of π0(Σ(1)) → π0(Σ(0)×Σ(0)) = I×I. Concretely, i ≤ j iff some arrow goes from a point of component i to a point of component j.

Proof on this page.
- Reflexivity comes from the identity section δ.
- Transitivity: suppose u: x→y with [x]=i, [y]=j, and v: y'→z with [y']=j, [z]=k. Since y and y' are only in the same component, the arrows are not composable as they stand. One needs π0(Σ(2)) → π0(Σ(1)) ×_{π0Σ(0)} π0(Σ(1)) to be surjective.
- This follows from the Lemma: given a cartesian square X' = X ×_Y Y' with f: X→Y a fibration, the map π0(X') → π0(X) ×_{π0 Y} π0(Y') is surjective. Proof: join f(x) to g(y') by a path, lift it starting at x, and the endpoint paired with y' lies in X'.

Consequence. Regard the preorder I as a discrete topological category (equivalently a simplicial nerve). There is then a canonical continuous functor φ: Σ → I, given by φ0: Σ(0) → I and φ1: Σ(1) → I1 = graph of ≤. Equivalently there are topological-sum decompositions
- Σ(0) = ⊔_i Σ_i,
- Σ(1) = ⊔_{i≤j} Σ_ij,
with s: Σ_ij → Σ_i, b: Σ_ij → Σ_j and δ(Σ_i) ⊂ Σ_ii. Compatibility with composition is automatic once φ is defined on components.

Where it leads. The next page adds conditions: b a proper immersion, the non-identity part rare, finite dimension. These force Σ_ii = Σ_i, so I becomes a genuine order and Σ is a 'directed' category over the poset of strata. This is a strict topological model of the stratification-as-category idea: the Σ_ij are the link bundles of the déploiement, fibred over the strata Σ_i and mapping to Σ_j.
errors: The decompositions Σ(0) = ⊔Σ_i as topological sums, and the continuity of φ0 into a discrete set, require the components of Σ(0) and Σ(1) to be open (e.g. local (path-)connectedness). This is not stated, though the margin NB seems to comment on what is used about the components.
π0 must mean path components, both for the Lemma (path lifting) and for π0(Σ0×Σ0) = π0Σ0×π0Σ0. With quasi-components the argument needs extra hypotheses.
Minor inconsistency: the previous page assumes s fibrant, while this page invokes 'b fibrant'. Either suffices by the symmetry of the Lemma, since Σ(2) is the fibre product of b and s.
Only a preorder is obtained here; antisymmetry needs the conditions of the next page.

ideas.what: Surjectivity of π0 of a homotopy-pullback-like square when one leg is a fibration (the Lemma)
ideas.modern_name: π0-surjectivity for pullbacks along fibrations (Mayer–Vietoris / long exact sequence at the π0 level)

ideas.what: Extracting the (pre)ordered set of strata as the image of π0(arrows) → π0(objects)², for a topological category with fibrant source/target
ideas.modern_name: poset of strata recovered from an exit-path category / the functor X → P in the 'stratified space = map to a poset' formalism
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths), Treumann 2009, Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses stratified spaces and 'dévissage', but not this categorical formalism explicitly as far as I know

ideas.what: Modelling a stratified space by a topological category Σ over the poset of strata, with link spaces Σ_ij fibred over Σ_i and mapping to Σ_j and composition Σ_ij×Σ_jk→Σ_ik (the 'déploiement')
ideas.modern_name: strict topological analogue of décollages / unzipped (resolved) stratified spaces / link-bundle (Mather control data) categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping, 2017), Barwick–Glasman–Haine (décollages, Exodromy, 2018+), Mather/Thom control data
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (déploiement/dévissage of stratified structures, described informally)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates stratified spaces as topological categories whose source/target are fibrations. The poset of strata emerges intrinsically from π0, with the canonical functor to it and the decomposition Σ(1)=⊔Σ_ij. With the next page's conditions (non-identity endo-arrows excluded on each stratum), this is a strict topological version of what is now called a décollage or a 'layered' category over a poset (BGH), or of AFT's unzipping. The intrinsic recovery of the stratifying poset from the category, rather than its being given a priori, is a point of view the modern literature usually does not adopt.
missed.quote: considérons la catégorie top. discrète associée à l'ens. préordonné I = π0(Σ0) ... On a alors un foncteur canonique de catégories topologiques Σ → I
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority (1981) for the categorical/exit-path viewpoint on stratifications. It may also suggest a point-set (strict, Segal-like) model for stratified homotopy types in which the poset is derived rather than imposed.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is elementary: a path-lifting lemma and the construction of a preorder. However, the framework — stratified spaces as topological categories over a poset of strata with fibrant structure maps and link spaces Σ_ij — anticipates exit-path/décollage/unzipping ideas of 2009–2019. It does so in unpublished notes that are, to my knowledge, not credited in that literature. The page itself is a routine step within that program.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the maps are π0(b) and π0(s), not π0(b_0) and π0(s_1); i.e. π0(Σ(2)) → (π0(Σ(1)),π0(b)) ×_{π0(Σ(0))} (π0(Σ(1)),π0(s)).
The crossed-out word in line 1 is 'symétrique', replaced by 'réflexive' (confirmed); the crossed-out start reads 'Cette posé' (or similar), replaced by 'Cette relation'.
I1 line: the final equality reads 'dans π0(Σ0)×π0(Σ0) = I×I' (the trailing '=I' in the transcription should be I×I; the end is partly cut off).
δ(x) = id^Σ_x (identity arrow of Σ at x), not 'id Σ_x'.
The margin note is roughly 'NB — on n'utilise pas que les composantes connexes de Σ0 et Σ1 ...' — uncertain, likely about openness/connectedness of components.
